## Load gene annotation maps
```{r}
# Extract GeneID to gene_symbol from NCBI genomic.gff
gff_lines <- readLines("genomic.gff")
gene_lines <- grep("\tgene\t", gff_lines, value = TRUE)

extract_geneid_symbol <- function(attr) {
  id <- sub(".*Dbxref=GeneID:([0-9]+).*", "\\1", attr)
  symbol <- sub(".*;gene=([^;]+);.*", "\\1", attr)
  data.frame(GeneID = id, gene_symbol = symbol)
}

gff_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(gene_lines, function(line) {
  fields <- strsplit(line, "\t")[[1]]
  if (length(fields) >= 9) extract_geneid_symbol(fields[9]) else NULL
}))

gff_df$GeneID <- as.character(gff_df$GeneID)


# Combine GFF and gene2ensembl mappings
gene_map <- gff_df %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

## create separate map for manually labeled LOC genes
loc_map <- c(
  "103040661" = "her4.1", #radial glia
  "103035120" = "gfap", #astrocytes/radial glia
  "103034161" = "mpeg1", #macrophage/microglia
  "125803969"= "mrc1b" #macrophage/microglia
)

## update map 
# Make sure GeneID is character to match loc_map names
gene_map$GeneID <- as.character(gene_map$GeneID)

# Replace gene_symbol where GeneID matches your manual map
gene_map$gene_symbol <- ifelse(
  gene_map$GeneID %in% names(loc_map),
  loc_map[gene_map$GeneID],
  gene_map$gene_symbol
)

# Check results
head(gene_map)
```
## define functions
### Run binomial glm for composition stats
Note: scCoda does not work well with low n data sets so we used a 
Binomial glm with dispersion and batch
-Runs binomial with batch correction first, tests overdispersion vs overdisp_cut, if above threshold, uses beta-binomial for stats
```{r}
run_prop_glm_and_plot <- function(
  denom_obj,
  group_var = "idents",           # "idents" or metadata column in denom_obj
  sample_col = "sample_id",
  pop_col = "population",
  batch_col = "batch",            # created from sample_id if missing
  pop_ref = "surface",
  pop_levels = c("surface", "cave"),
  plot_percent = TRUE,
  bar_error = c("sem", "sd", "none"),
  overlay_points = TRUE,
  point_jitter = 0.08,
  fdr_cutoff = 0.05,
  glm_family = c("auto", "betabinomial", "quasibinomial", "binomial"),
  overdisp_cut = 1.2,
  # ---- batch-driven overdispersion revert gate (AUTO only) ----
  batch_revert = TRUE,
  batch_revert_ratio = 0.6,       # if overdisp_with_batch <= ratio * overdisp_no_batch -> "mostly batch"
  batch_revert_p = 0.05,          # batch must be supported by binomial LRT
  batch_revert_overdisp_max = 1.5,# and residual overdisp w/ batch must be modest
  order_levels = NULL,
  strict_sum_to_one = TRUE
) {
  bar_error  <- match.arg(bar_error)
  glm_family <- match.arg(glm_family)

  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(Seurat)
    library(dplyr)
    library(tidyr)
    library(ggplot2)
    library(purrr)
    library(broom)
  })

  md <- as.data.frame(denom_obj@meta.data)

  if (!all(c(sample_col, pop_col) %in% colnames(md))) {
    stop("Metadata must contain: ", paste(c(sample_col, pop_col), collapse = ", "))
  }

  # unwrap list columns (defensive)
  for (v in c(sample_col, pop_col)) {
    if (is.list(md[[v]])) md[[v]] <- vapply(md[[v]], \(x) as.character(x)[1], character(1))
  }
  if (!identical(group_var, "idents") && group_var %in% colnames(md) && is.list(md[[group_var]])) {
    md[[group_var]] <- vapply(md[[group_var]], \(x) as.character(x)[1], character(1))
  }

  # factorize sample + population
  md[[sample_col]] <- factor(md[[sample_col]])
  md[[pop_col]]    <- stats::relevel(factor(md[[pop_col]], levels = pop_levels), ref = pop_ref)

  # ============================================================
  # Batch: derive from sample_id (underscore => batch2; else batch1)
  # ============================================================
  smp_chr <- as.character(md[[sample_col]])
  md[[batch_col]] <- ifelse(grepl("_", smp_chr), "batch2", "batch1")
  md[[batch_col]] <- factor(md[[batch_col]], levels = c("batch1", "batch2"))

  # group labels from THIS SAME OBJECT
  if (identical(group_var, "idents")) {
    grp <- as.character(Idents(denom_obj))
    default_levels <- levels(Idents(denom_obj))
  } else {
    if (!group_var %in% colnames(md)) stop("group_var not found in metadata: ", group_var)
    grp <- as.character(md[[group_var]])
    default_levels <- if (is.factor(md[[group_var]])) levels(md[[group_var]]) else unique(grp)
  }

  # enforce complete labeling (no silent dropping)
  if (any(is.na(grp) | grp == "")) {
    bad_n <- sum(is.na(grp) | grp == "")
    stop(
      "Found ", bad_n, " cells with NA/blank group labels in ", group_var, ".\n",
      "Fix labels so proportions are well-defined."
    )
  }

  md$.__group <- as.character(grp)

  # determine plotting order
  keep_levels <- if (!is.null(order_levels)) as.character(order_levels) else as.character(default_levels)
  present <- unique(md$.__group)
  if (!all(present %in% keep_levels)) keep_levels <- c(keep_levels, setdiff(present, keep_levels))
  keep_levels <- keep_levels[keep_levels != "" & !is.na(keep_levels)]
  md$.__group <- factor(md$.__group, levels = keep_levels)

  # ============================================================
  # 1) Per-sample counts and proportions
  # ============================================================
  totals <- md %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[sample_col]], .data[[pop_col]], .data[[batch_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(total = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

  counts <- md %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[sample_col]], .data[[pop_col]], .data[[batch_col]], .__group) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

  props_by_sample <- totals %>%
    tidyr::expand_grid(.__group = factor(keep_levels, levels = keep_levels)) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(counts, by = c(sample_col, pop_col, batch_col, ".__group")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      count = ifelse(is.na(count), 0L, count),
      non   = total - count,
      prop  = count / total
    )

  if (any(props_by_sample$non < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    stop("Some group counts exceeded totals (should not happen with one input object).")
  }

  qc_sumprop <- props_by_sample %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[sample_col]], .data[[pop_col]], .data[[batch_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(sum_prop = sum(prop), .groups = "drop")

  if (isTRUE(strict_sum_to_one)) {
    if (any(abs(qc_sumprop$sum_prop - 1) > 1e-6)) {
      print(qc_sumprop)
      stop(
        "Proportions do not sum to 1 within at least one (sample, population, batch).\n",
        "This indicates grouping does not partition all cells in the object."
      )
    }
  }

  # ============================================================
  # 2) Bars + error bars across samples
  # ============================================================
  bar_df <- props_by_sample %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.__group, .data[[pop_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      mean_prop = mean(prop, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_prop   = sd(prop, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_samp    = dplyr::n(),
      se_prop   = sd_prop / sqrt(n_samp),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Var1 = factor(as.character(.__group), levels = keep_levels),
      Var2 = factor(as.character(.data[[pop_col]]), levels = pop_levels)
    )

  cellprops <- bar_df %>% dplyr::transmute(Var1, Var2, Freq = mean_prop)

  # ============================================================
  # 3) Effects per group (population cave vs surface)
  # ============================================================
  pop_term <- paste0(pop_col, pop_levels[2])  # e.g. "populationcave"

  # Robust beta-binomial fitter (tries multiple glmmTMBControl settings)
  fit_bb_robust <- function(form, data) {
    if (!requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly = TRUE)) {
      stop("glm_family includes betabinomial but 'glmmTMB' is not installed.")
    }

    ctrl_list <- list(
      glmmTMB::glmmTMBControl(),
      glmmTMB::glmmTMBControl(
        optimizer = stats::nlminb,
        optCtrl = list(iter.max = 100000, eval.max = 100000)
      ),
      glmmTMB::glmmTMBControl(
        optimizer = stats::optim,
        optArgs = list(method = "BFGS"),
        optCtrl = list(maxit = 100000)
      )
    )

    fits <- vector("list", length(ctrl_list))
    diags <- vector("list", length(ctrl_list))

    for (i in seq_along(ctrl_list)) {
      warn_msgs <- character(0)

      fit_i <- tryCatch(
        withCallingHandlers(
          glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
            form,
            family = glmmTMB::betabinomial(link = "logit"),
            data = data,
            control = ctrl_list[[i]]
          ),
          warning = function(w) {
            warn_msgs <<- c(warn_msgs, conditionMessage(w))
            invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
          }
        ),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )

      if (is.null(fit_i)) {
        fits[[i]] <- NULL
        diags[[i]] <- list(ok = FALSE, warn = "ERROR", conv = NA_integer_, pdHess = NA, aic = Inf)
        next
      }

      conv_code <- tryCatch(fit_i$fit$convergence, error = function(e) NA_integer_)
      pdHess    <- tryCatch(isTRUE(fit_i$sdr$pdHess), error = function(e) NA)
      aic_val   <- tryCatch(stats::AIC(fit_i), error = function(e) Inf)

      ok <- isTRUE(pdHess) && (!is.na(conv_code) && conv_code == 0)

      fits[[i]] <- fit_i
      diags[[i]] <- list(
        ok = ok,
        warn = if (length(warn_msgs) > 0) paste(unique(warn_msgs), collapse = " | ") else NA_character_,
        conv = conv_code,
        pdHess = pdHess,
        aic = aic_val
      )

      if (ok) return(list(fit = fit_i, diag = diags[[i]]))
    }

    aic_vec <- vapply(diags, function(d) {
      if (is.null(d) || is.null(d$aic) || !is.finite(d$aic)) Inf else d$aic
    }, numeric(1))

    if (all(is.infinite(aic_vec)) || all(vapply(fits, is.null, logical(1)))) {
      return(list(
        fit = NULL,
        diag = list(ok = FALSE, warn = "ALL_FITS_FAILED", conv = NA_integer_, pdHess = NA, aic = Inf)
      ))
    }

    best_i <- which.min(aic_vec)
    list(fit = fits[[best_i]], diag = diags[[best_i]])
  }

  fit_and_tidy_one <- function(df_sub) {
    form_full <- stats::as.formula(paste0("cbind(count, non) ~ ", pop_col, " + ", batch_col))

    # ---- Always fit binomial baseline (for overdisp diagnostic + binomial output) ----
    m_bin <- stats::glm(form_full, family = stats::binomial(), data = df_sub)
    overdisp_bin <- m_bin$deviance / m_bin$df.residual

    tidy_bin <- broom::tidy(m_bin) %>%
      dplyr::filter(term == pop_term) %>%
      dplyr::transmute(
        term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value,
        dispersion = 1,
        overdisp   = overdisp_bin,
        model_used = "binomial"
      )

    if (nrow(tidy_bin) == 0) {
      tidy_bin <- dplyr::tibble(
        term = pop_term, estimate = NA_real_, std.error = NA_real_,
        statistic = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_,
        dispersion = 1, overdisp = overdisp_bin,
        model_used = "binomial"
      )
    }

    # If binomial explicitly requested -> return it
    if (glm_family == "binomial") return(tidy_bin)

    # Quasi helper (used for explicit quasi or auto fallback)
    fit_quasi_row <- function(label = "quasibinomial") {
      m_q <- stats::glm(form_full, family = stats::quasibinomial(), data = df_sub)
      disp_q <- summary(m_q)$dispersion
      over_q <- m_q$deviance / m_q$df.residual

      td <- broom::tidy(m_q)
      out <- td %>%
        dplyr::filter(term == pop_term) %>%
        dplyr::transmute(
          term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value,
          dispersion = disp_q,
          overdisp   = over_q,
          model_used = label
        )

      if (nrow(out) == 0) {
        out <- dplyr::tibble(
          term = pop_term, estimate = NA_real_, std.error = NA_real_,
          statistic = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_,
          dispersion = disp_q, overdisp = over_q,
          model_used = label
        )
      }
      out
    }

    if (glm_family == "quasibinomial") return(fit_quasi_row("quasibinomial"))

    # ============================================================
    # AUTO-only "batch explains overdispersion" revert-to-binomial
    # ============================================================
    if (glm_family == "auto" && isTRUE(batch_revert)) {
      form_nobatch <- stats::as.formula(paste0("cbind(count, non) ~ ", pop_col))
      m_nobatch <- stats::glm(form_nobatch, family = stats::binomial(), data = df_sub)
      overdisp_nobatch <- m_nobatch$deviance / m_nobatch$df.residual

      lrt_b <- stats::anova(m_nobatch, m_bin, test = "Chisq")
      p_batch <- NA_real_
      pcol <- intersect(colnames(lrt_b), c("Pr(>Chi)", "Pr(>Chisq)"))
      if (length(pcol) > 0) p_batch <- unname(lrt_b[[pcol[1]]][2])

      ratio <- overdisp_bin / overdisp_nobatch

      if (is.finite(overdisp_nobatch) && is.finite(overdisp_bin) && is.finite(ratio) &&
          (overdisp_nobatch > overdisp_cut) &&
          (ratio <= batch_revert_ratio) &&
          (!is.na(p_batch) && p_batch < batch_revert_p) &&
          (overdisp_bin <= batch_revert_overdisp_max)) {
        tidy_bin$model_used <- "binomial_batch_explains"
        return(tidy_bin)
      }
    }

    # AUTO: if not meaningfully overdispersed, stick with binomial
    if (glm_family == "auto" && is.finite(overdisp_bin) && overdisp_bin <= overdisp_cut) {
      return(tidy_bin)
    }

    # From here: we want beta-binomial (explicit or auto when overdispersed)
    if (!requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly = TRUE)) {
      if (glm_family == "auto") return(fit_quasi_row("quasi_fallback"))
      stop("glm_family='betabinomial' requires 'glmmTMB'. Install it with install.packages('glmmTMB').")
    }

    bb_full <- fit_bb_robust(form_full, df_sub)
    m_full  <- bb_full$fit
    d_full  <- bb_full$diag

    # If beta cannot be fit, AUTO falls back to quasi; explicit beta returns NAs
    if (is.null(m_full)) {
      if (glm_family == "auto") {
        out <- fit_quasi_row("quasi_fallback")
        out$bb_conv   <- d_full$conv
        out$bb_pdHess <- d_full$pdHess
        out$bb_warn   <- d_full$warn
        return(out)
      }
      return(dplyr::tibble(
        term = pop_term, estimate = NA_real_, std.error = NA_real_,
        statistic = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_,
        dispersion = NA_real_, overdisp = overdisp_bin,
        model_used = "betabinomial_failed",
        bb_conv = d_full$conv, bb_pdHess = d_full$pdHess, bb_warn = d_full$warn
      ))
    }

    # ============================================================
    # WALD inference for beta-binomial (matches binomial reporting)
    # ============================================================
    co <- summary(m_full)$coefficients$cond
    co_pop <- co[rownames(co) == pop_term, , drop = FALSE]

    est <- if (nrow(co_pop) == 1) unname(co_pop[1, "Estimate"]) else NA_real_
    se  <- if (nrow(co_pop) == 1) unname(co_pop[1, "Std. Error"]) else NA_real_
    z   <- if (nrow(co_pop) == 1 && "z value" %in% colnames(co_pop)) unname(co_pop[1, "z value"]) else NA_real_
    p_w <- if (nrow(co_pop) == 1 && "Pr(>|z|)" %in% colnames(co_pop)) unname(co_pop[1, "Pr(>|z|)"]) else NA_real_

    bb_sigma <- tryCatch(unname(stats::sigma(m_full)), error = function(e) NA_real_)

    out <- dplyr::tibble(
      term       = pop_term,
      estimate   = est,
      std.error  = se,
      statistic  = z,
      p.value    = p_w,
      dispersion = bb_sigma,
      overdisp   = overdisp_bin,
      model_used = "betabinomial",
      bb_conv    = d_full$conv,
      bb_pdHess  = d_full$pdHess,
      bb_warn    = d_full$warn
    )

    # Some fits can return NA Wald SE/p even if pdHess TRUE; AUTO falls back to quasi.
    if (glm_family == "auto" && (!is.finite(out$std.error) || !is.finite(out$p.value))) {
      qout <- fit_quasi_row("quasi_fallback")
      qout$bb_conv   <- d_full$conv
      qout$bb_pdHess <- d_full$pdHess
      qout$bb_warn   <- d_full$warn
      return(qout)
    }

    out
  }

  glm_effects <- props_by_sample %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.__group) %>%
    tidyr::nest() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(tidy = purrr::map(data, fit_and_tidy_one)) %>%
    dplyr::select(.__group, tidy) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(tidy) %>%
    {
      if (!"bb_conv" %in% names(.)) {
        .$bb_conv   <- NA_integer_
        .$bb_pdHess <- NA
        .$bb_warn   <- NA_character_
      }
      if (!"model_used" %in% names(.)) {
        .$model_used <- NA_character_
      }
      .
    } %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
      p_adj = stats::p.adjust(p.value, "fdr"),
      sig = ifelse(p_adj < fdr_cutoff, paste0("FDR < ", fdr_cutoff), "NS")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      group = as.character(.__group),
      term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value,
      dispersion, overdisp,
      p_adj, odds_ratio, sig,
      model_used,
      bb_conv, bb_pdHess, bb_warn
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(p.value)

  # ============================================================
  # 4) Plot: bars + error bars + optional sample points
  # ============================================================
  ymult <- if (plot_percent) 100 else 1
  ylab  <- if (plot_percent) "Percentage composition" else "Proportion composition"

  p <- ggplot(cellprops, aes(fill = Var2, y = Freq * ymult, x = Var1)) +
    geom_bar(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), stat = "identity") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Cell type", y = ylab, fill = "population") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkseagreen3", "palevioletred"))

  if (bar_error != "none") {
    p <- p +
      geom_errorbar(
        data = bar_df,
        aes(
          x = Var1,
          ymin = (mean_prop - if (bar_error == "sem") se_prop else sd_prop) * ymult,
          ymax = (mean_prop + if (bar_error == "sem") se_prop else sd_prop) * ymult,
          group = Var2
        ),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        color = "black",
        linewidth = 0.4,
        width = 0.25,
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)
      )
  }

  if (isTRUE(overlay_points)) {
    p <- p +
      geom_point(
        data = props_by_sample %>%
          dplyr::mutate(
            Var1 = factor(as.character(.__group), levels = keep_levels),
            Var2 = factor(as.character(.data[[pop_col]]), levels = pop_levels)
          ),
        aes(x = Var1, y = prop * ymult, fill = Var2),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        shape = 21,
        color = "black",
        size = 2,
        alpha = 0.8,
        position = position_jitterdodge(
          jitter.width = point_jitter,
          dodge.width  = 0.9
        )
      )
  }

  list(
    plot_bar = p,
    glm_effects = glm_effects,
    props_by_sample = props_by_sample,
    cellprops = cellprops,
    bar_df = bar_df,
    qc_sumprop = qc_sumprop,
    glm_family = glm_family,
    overdisp_cut = overdisp_cut
  )
}
```

### Pseudobulk DEGs 
#### Annotation - DEGs across cell types
```{r}
deseq2_pb_annotation <- function(
  cts,
  coldata,
  target_celltype,
  ref_celltypes = NULL,
  fdr_explore = 0.20,
  min_total_count = 10,
  min_samples = 2
) {

  stopifnot(is.matrix(cts) || inherits(cts, "dgCMatrix"))
  stopifnot(all(c("col_id","sample","Population","CellType") %in% colnames(coldata)))

  # clean coldata
  coldata <- as.data.frame(coldata, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  coldata$col_id     <- as.character(coldata$col_id)
  coldata$sample     <- as.character(coldata$sample)
  coldata$Population <- as.character(coldata$Population)
  coldata$CellType   <- as.character(coldata$CellType)

  # USE BOTH POPULATIONS for annotation (no subsetting)
  cd <- coldata
  if (nrow(cd) == 0) stop("coldata is empty after cleaning.")

  # optionally restrict which “other” celltypes are allowed
  if (!is.null(ref_celltypes)) {
    keep_cts <- unique(c(ref_celltypes, target_celltype))
    cd <- cd[cd$CellType %in% keep_cts, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(cd) == 0) stop("After ref_celltypes filtering, nothing left.")
  }

  # need at least some target samples
  if (!any(cd$CellType == target_celltype)) {
    stop("No pseudobulk columns for target celltype: ", target_celltype)
  }

  # align counts to cd
  stopifnot(all(cd$col_id %in% colnames(cts)))
  cts2 <- cts[, cd$col_id, drop = FALSE]

  # define target vs other
  cd$is_target <- ifelse(cd$CellType == target_celltype, "target", "other")
  cd$is_target <- factor(cd$is_target, levels = c("other","target"))

  # Prefilter genes: expressed in at least min_samples pseudobulk columns at >= min_total_count
  keep <- Matrix::rowSums(cts2 >= min_total_count) >= min_samples
  cts2 <- cts2[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(cts2) == 0) stop("All genes filtered out; relax thresholds.")

  # DESeq2 colData must match column order
  cd2 <- cd[match(colnames(cts2), cd$col_id), , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(cts2), cd2$col_id))
  rownames(cd2) <- cd2$col_id

  # IMPORTANT: sample as a blocking factor (paired within sample)
  cd2$sample    <- factor(cd2$sample)
  cd2$is_target <- factor(cd2$is_target, levels = c("other","target"))

  dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = round(cts2),
    colData   = cd2,
    design    = ~ sample + is_target
  )

  # sanity: need both target and other
  if (length(unique(cd2$is_target)) < 2) {
    stop("Need both target and other columns after filtering.")
  }

  dds <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds)

  # results for target vs other
  res <- DESeq2::results(
    dds,
    contrast = c("is_target","target","other"),
    alpha = fdr_explore
  ) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("gene")

  res_all <- res |>
    dplyr::arrange(padj, dplyr::desc(baseMean))

  res_sig <- res_all |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj), padj < fdr_explore)

  list(
    dds             = dds,
    res_sig         = res_sig,
    res_all         = res_all,
    target_celltype = target_celltype,
    fdr_explore     = fdr_explore
  )
}
```
##### Export single cell type significant DEGs to csv
```{r}
format_and_write_annotation_csv <- function(
  res_df,
  neuro_cluster_label,          # e.g. "e2_tectum"
  padj_cut = 0.05,
  lfc_abs_min = 0,
  top_n = 100,
  drop_LOC = TRUE,
  loc_regex = "^LOC",
  extra_drop_regex = NULL
) {

  stopifnot(all(c("gene","padj","baseMean") %in% colnames(res_df)))

  df <- res_df

  # Optional filtering of LOC / unwanted symbols
  if (drop_LOC) {
    df <- df %>% filter(!grepl(loc_regex, gene))
  }
  if (!is.null(extra_drop_regex)) {
    df <- df %>% filter(!grepl(extra_drop_regex, gene))
  }

  # Keep significant genes
  df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(padj), padj <= padj_cut)

  # Determine which LFC column to use
  lfc_col <- if ("log2FoldChange_shrunk" %in% colnames(df)) {
    "log2FoldChange_shrunk"
  } else if ("log2FoldChange" %in% colnames(df)) {
    "log2FoldChange"
  } else {
    stop("res_df must contain log2FoldChange or log2FoldChange_shrunk")
  }

  # Keep only TARGET-ENRICHED genes
  df <- df %>% filter(.data[[lfc_col]] > 0)

  # Optional LFC threshold
  if (lfc_abs_min > 0) {
    df <- df %>% filter(abs(.data[[lfc_col]]) >= lfc_abs_min)
  }

  # Add direction column (useful for sanity checks)
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(direction = "Up in target")

  # Rank by: significance → specificity → expression
  df_out <- df %>%
    arrange(padj, desc(abs(.data[[lfc_col]])), desc(baseMean)) %>%
    slice_head(n = top_n)

  # Column order (clean CSV)
  preferred <- c("gene","baseMean",lfc_col,"padj","pvalue","stat","lfcSE","direction")
  keep_cols <- c(preferred, setdiff(colnames(df_out), preferred))
  df_out <- df_out %>% select(any_of(keep_cols))

  # Write directly to WORKING DIRECTORY
  fname <- paste0(neuro_cluster_label, ".csv")
  readr::write_csv(df_out, fname)

  message("Wrote annotation DEG CSV to: ", normalizePath(fname))

  return(df_out)
}
```
##### Export all cell type markers with log2fold change cutoff
```{r}
run_all_celltype_deg_exports <- function(
  cts,
  coldata,
  padj_cut = 0.05,
  lfc_min = 1,
  positive_only = TRUE,
  out_csv = "AllCellTypes_DEGs_filtered.csv",
  verbose = TRUE
) {
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(dplyr)
    library(readr)
  })

  stopifnot(is.matrix(cts) || inherits(cts, "dgCMatrix"))
  stopifnot(all(c("col_id","sample","Population","CellType") %in% colnames(coldata)))

  cd <- as.data.frame(coldata, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  celltypes <- sort(unique(cd$CellType))
  celltypes <- celltypes[!is.na(celltypes) & celltypes != ""]

  if (length(celltypes) == 0) stop("No celltypes found in coldata.")

  results_list <- vector("list", length(celltypes))
  names(results_list) <- celltypes

  failures <- list()

  for (ct in celltypes) {
    if (isTRUE(verbose)) message("Running DESeq2 for: ", ct)

    out <- try(
      deseq2_pb_annotation(
        cts = cts,
        coldata = cd,
        target_celltype = ct
      ),
      silent = TRUE
    )

    if (inherits(out, "try-error")) {
      failures[[ct]] <- as.character(out)
      next
    }

    df <- out$res_all %>%
      mutate(celltype = ct) %>%
      select(celltype, gene, padj, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue, baseMean) %>%
      filter(!is.na(padj), padj <= padj_cut) %>%
      filter(!is.na(log2FoldChange))

    if (positive_only) {
      df <- df %>%
        filter(log2FoldChange >= lfc_min)
    } else {
      df <- df %>%
        filter(abs(log2FoldChange) >= lfc_min)
    }

    df <- df %>%
      arrange(celltype, desc(log2FoldChange), padj, desc(baseMean))

    results_list[[ct]] <- df
  }

  combined_results <- bind_rows(results_list)

  readr::write_csv(combined_results, out_csv)

  if (isTRUE(verbose)) {
    message("Wrote filtered DEG file: ", normalizePath(out_csv))
    if (length(failures) > 0) {
      message("Some cell types failed. Check returned $failures.")
    }
  }

  return(list(
    degs = combined_results,
    failures = failures
  ))
}
```

#### Population - subset to cell type for surface vs cave
##### pseudobulk with deseq2
```{r}
deseq2_pb_celltype <- function(cts, coldata, celltype,
                               fdr_explore = 0.20,
                               min_total_count = 10,
                               min_samples = 2,
                               shrink_type = c("apeglm", "ashr", "normal")) {

  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(Matrix)
    library(DESeq2)
    library(dplyr)
    library(tibble)
  })

  shrink_type <- match.arg(shrink_type)

  stopifnot(is.matrix(cts) || inherits(cts, "dgCMatrix"))
  stopifnot(all(c("col_id","sample","Population","CellType") %in% colnames(coldata)))

  # Coerce to plain data.frame to avoid Rle/list columns breaking dplyr verbs
  coldata <- as.data.frame(coldata, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  coldata$col_id     <- as.character(coldata$col_id)
  coldata$sample     <- as.character(coldata$sample)
  coldata$Population <- as.character(coldata$Population)
  coldata$CellType   <- as.character(coldata$CellType)

  # Align count columns
  stopifnot(all(coldata$col_id %in% colnames(cts)))
  cts <- cts[, coldata$col_id, drop = FALSE]

  # Subset to the requested cell type (already pseudobulked columns)
  cd_ct <- coldata[coldata$CellType == celltype, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(cd_ct) == 0) stop("No pseudobulk samples for celltype: ", celltype)

  cts_ct <- cts[, cd_ct$col_id, drop = FALSE]

  # Prefilter genes
  keep <- Matrix::rowSums(cts_ct >= min_total_count) >= min_samples
  cts_ct <- cts_ct[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(cts_ct) == 0) stop("All genes filtered out; relax thresholds.")

  # Build DESeq2 colData and reorder to match columns
  cd_ct2 <- unique(cd_ct[, c("col_id", "sample", "Population")])
  cd_ct2 <- cd_ct2[match(colnames(cts_ct), cd_ct2$col_id), , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(cts_ct), cd_ct2$col_id))
  rownames(cd_ct2) <- cd_ct2$col_id

  # DESeq2
  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = round(cts_ct),
    colData   = cd_ct2,
    design    = ~ Population
  )

  dds$Population <- factor(dds$Population)
  if (!("surface" %in% levels(dds$Population))) {
    stop("Population must include 'surface'. Found: ", paste(levels(dds$Population), collapse = ", "))
  }
  if (length(levels(dds$Population)) != 2) {
    stop("This function assumes exactly 2 Population levels. Found: ", paste(levels(dds$Population), collapse = ", "))
  }

  dds$Population <- relevel(dds$Population, ref = "surface")
  dds <- DESeq(dds)

  alt <- setdiff(levels(dds$Population), "surface")[1]
  coef_name <- paste0("Population_", make.names(alt), "_vs_surface")
  if (!coef_name %in% resultsNames(dds)) {
    coef_name <- resultsNames(dds)[grepl("^Population_", resultsNames(dds))][1]
  }

  res <- results(dds, name = coef_name, alpha = fdr_explore) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("gene")

  res_shr <- tryCatch({
    shr <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = coef_name, type = shrink_type)
    as.data.frame(shr) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("gene")
  }, error = function(e) {
    shr <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = coef_name, type = "normal")
    as.data.frame(shr) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("gene")
  })

  res_merged <- res |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      res_shr |> dplyr::select(gene, log2FoldChange) |> dplyr::rename(log2FoldChange_shrunk = log2FoldChange),
      by = "gene"
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(padj, dplyr::desc(abs(log2FoldChange_shrunk)))

  res_celltype <- res_merged |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj), padj < fdr_explore)

  list(
    dds          = dds,
    res_celltype = res_celltype,
    res_all      = res_merged,
    celltype     = celltype,
    coef_name    = coef_name,
    fdr_explore  = fdr_explore
  )
}
```
label volcano plot
```{r}
label_top_genes <- function(de_result,
                            logfc_thresh = 0,
                            padj_thresh  = 0.05,
                            top_n_per_side = 80) {
  df <- de_result %>%
    mutate(
      # significance category for plotting
      significance = case_when(
        !is.na(padj) & padj < padj_thresh & log2FoldChange >  logfc_thresh ~ "Up in Cave",
        !is.na(padj) & padj < padj_thresh & log2FoldChange < -logfc_thresh ~ "Up in Surface",
        TRUE ~ "Not significant"
      ),
      # robust -log10(padj): guard against 0/NA
      logP = -log10(pmax(padj, .Machine$double.xmin)),

      # annotated = not LOC######## 
      is_annotated = !grepl("^LOC\\d+$", final_gene_symbol)
    )

  # choose which points to label: top N per side by -log10(padj), annotated only
  lab_idx <- df %>%
    filter(significance != "Not significant", is_annotated) %>%
    group_by(significance) %>%
    slice_max(order_by = logP, n = top_n_per_side, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(to_label = TRUE) %>%
    select(final_gene_symbol, log2FoldChange, padj, to_label)

  # attach labels; no join on floats for everything—only to mark the chosen labels
  df <- df %>%
    left_join(lab_idx,
              by = c("final_gene_symbol","log2FoldChange","padj")) %>%
    mutate(
      label = ifelse(!is.na(to_label), final_gene_symbol, NA_character_)
    ) %>%
    select(-to_label)

  df
}
```
##### MAST with FindMarkers
```{r}
run_celltype_DE_analysis_pop_fm <- function(
  seurat_obj,
  celltype_name,
  celltype_col = "gliacelltypes",
  pop_col = "population",
  assay_use = "RNA",
  layer_use = "data",
  cave_label = "cave",
  surface_label = "surface"
) {
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(Seurat)
    library(dplyr)
  })


  # Basic checks
  if (!inherits(seurat_obj, "Seurat")) {
    stop("seurat_obj must be a Seurat object")
  }

  md <- seurat_obj@meta.data

  if (!celltype_col %in% colnames(md)) {
    stop(sprintf("metadata column '%s' not found in seurat_obj@meta.data", celltype_col))
  }

  if (!pop_col %in% colnames(md)) {
    stop(sprintf("metadata column '%s' not found in seurat_obj@meta.data", pop_col))
  }

  if (!layer_use %in% Layers(seurat_obj[[assay_use]])) {
    stop(sprintf("layer '%s' not found in assay '%s'", layer_use, assay_use))
  }

 
  # Subset to requested cell type
   keep_cells <- rownames(md)[
    !is.na(md[[celltype_col]]) &
      md[[celltype_col]] == celltype_name
   ]

  if (length(keep_cells) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("No cells found for cell type '%s'", celltype_name))
  }

  obj_sub <- subset(seurat_obj, cells = keep_cells)

 
  # Confirm both populations are present
  sub_pops <- unique(as.character(obj_sub@meta.data[[pop_col]]))

  if (!all(c(cave_label, surface_label) %in% sub_pops)) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "Cell type '%s' does not contain both '%s' and '%s'",
      celltype_name, cave_label, surface_label
    ))
  }

 
  # Set assay and identities
  DefaultAssay(obj_sub) <- assay_use
  Idents(obj_sub) <- factor(obj_sub@meta.data[[pop_col]], levels = c(surface_label, cave_label))

  # Set latent vars if present
  ncount_var   <- paste0("nCount_", assay_use)
  nfeature_var <- paste0("nFeature_", assay_use)

  latent_vars_use <- c(ncount_var, nfeature_var)
  latent_vars_use <- latent_vars_use[latent_vars_use %in% colnames(obj_sub@meta.data)]

  if (length(latent_vars_use) == 0) {
    latent_vars_use <- NULL
  }

 
  # Run DE
  #    ident.1 = cave, ident.2 = surface
  #    positive log2FC = Up in Cave
  de_result <- FindMarkers(
    object = obj_sub,
    ident.1 = cave_label,
    ident.2 = surface_label,
    assay = assay_use,
    slot = layer_use,
    test.use = "MAST",
    min.pct = 0,
    logfc.threshold = 0,
    only.pos = FALSE,
    only.variable.features = FALSE,
    latent.vars = latent_vars_use,
    verbose = TRUE
  )

  
  # Add gene column + labels
  de_result$gene <- rownames(de_result)

  de_result <- de_result %>%
    mutate(
      celltype = celltype_name,
      significance = case_when(
        p_val_adj < 0.05 & avg_log2FC > 0 ~ "Up in Cave",
        p_val_adj < 0.05 & avg_log2FC < 0 ~ "Up in Surface",
        TRUE ~ "Not significant"
      )
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(avg_log2FC))

  return(de_result)
}
```

### Plotting
```{r}
mini_axis_umap <- function(
  seurat_obj,
  reduction = "umap",
  group.by = NULL,
  split.by = NULL,
  label = TRUE,
  shuffle = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.8,
  pt.size = 0.5,
  axis_frac = 0.08,
  pad_frac  = 0.03,
  arrow_mm  = 2,
  linewidth = 0.5,
  add_labels = TRUE,
  label_x = "UMAP 1",
  label_y = "UMAP 2",
  label_size = 3,
  margin_mm = 5.5,
  seed = NULL
) {
  stopifnot(inherits(seurat_obj, "Seurat"))

  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)

  # 1) Base DimPlot
  p <- DimPlot(
    seurat_obj,
    reduction = reduction,
    group.by = group.by,
    split.by = split.by,
    label = label,
    shuffle = shuffle,
    alpha = alpha,
    pt.size = pt.size
  ) + NoLegend()

  # 2) Remove axes completely
  p_clean <- p +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(margin_mm, margin_mm, margin_mm, margin_mm, unit = "mm")) +
    NoLegend()

  # 3) Compute panel ranges
  gb <- ggplot_build(p_clean)
  pp <- gb$layout$panel_params[[1]]
  x_rng <- pp$x.range
  y_rng <- pp$y.range

  x_span <- diff(x_rng)
  y_span <- diff(y_rng)

  # Bottom-left corner position (with padding)
  x0 <- x_rng[1] + pad_frac * x_span
  y0 <- y_rng[1] + pad_frac * y_span

  # Mini-axis lengths
  dx <- axis_frac * x_span
  dy <- axis_frac * y_span

  # 4) Add mini-axes + optional labels
  p_final <- p_clean +
    annotate(
      "segment",
      x = x0, xend = x0 + dx,
      y = y0, yend = y0,
      linewidth = linewidth,
      arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(arrow_mm, "mm"))
    ) +
    annotate(
      "segment",
      x = x0, xend = x0,
      y = y0, yend = y0 + dy,
      linewidth = linewidth,
      arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(arrow_mm, "mm"))
    )

  if (isTRUE(add_labels)) {
    p_final <- p_final +
      annotate(
        "text",
        x = x0 + dx, y = y0 - 0.01 * y_span,
        label = label_x, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = label_size
      ) +
      annotate(
        "text",
        x = x0 - 0.01 * x_span, y = y0 + dy,
        label = label_y, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, angle = 90, size = label_size
      )
  }

  return(p_final)
}
```

# . Annotate by cluster
## Cluster 0: Tectal Ventricular Zone radial glia

One-line identity: Cycling radial glia-like ventricular zone progenitors of the dorsal midbrain/optic tectum, defined by a strong mitotic and DNA-replication program along with tectal progenitor patterning genes and Notch-associated neural stem cell features (de Oliveira-Carlos et al., 2013; Matsunaga et al., 2001; Pose-Méndez et al., 2024; Thomas et al., 2006; Wong et al., 2010; Yu & He, 2019).  
 
**Key evidence**

  • Definitive cycling ventricular-zone progenitor program: mki67, pcna, ccnd1, cdk1, cdk2, plk1, top2a,
  bub1, nuf2, kif11, kif23, aspm, anln, mcm2, mcm7, pole, pole2, prim2, dnmt1, brip1, bard1
    → The dominant signal in this cluster is active cell cycling, including genes that code for DNA
    replication, chromosome segregation, and genome maintenance. 
 
  • Radial glia identity: notch1a, her8.2, foxn4, nr2e1, sox2
    → Notch-associated stem cell markers support annotation as radial glia-like neural
    stem/progenitor cells positioned at the ventricle. 
 
  • Dorsal midbrain / tectal progenitor patterning program: pax7a, pax7b, pax3a, dmbx1a, dmbx1b, otx2b, zic3,
  zic6, tenm3, plxnb3, efemp1
    → These genes anchor the cluster to a dorsal mesencephalic/tectal progenitor identity rather than a
    generic forebrain or hindbrain VZ. Ax7/pax3 are classic tectal regionalization genes, while dmbx1 genes
    are directly implicated in zebrafish midbrain progenitor proliferation and differentiation.  

  • Neurogenic but still progenitor-biased state: foxn4, sox11b, myt1a, ebf2, bcl11aa, tox, cbfa2t2
    → This cluster is not simply quiescent radial glia. It carries a neurogenic transcriptional program
    layered onto the VZ stem/progenitor state, consistent with cycling tectal radial glia and early
    neurogenic progenitors within the ventricular zone.  
 
  • Growth factor and morphogen responsiveness consistent with ventricular progenitors: ctnnb1, fsta, fstl1a,
  plxnb3, efemp1
    → These genes reinforce a patterning-responsive tectal VZ state that receives and interprets
    developmental signaling cues.

**Decision rule:** 

The combined presence of a strong mitotic ventricular-zone program, radial glia / neural stem cell markers, and dorsal midbrain/tectal patterning genes supports annotation as tectal ventricular zone radial glia.  

**Distinguishing note:**

This cluster is distinguished from non-cycling radial glia by its very strong cell-cycle and DNA-replication signature, and from non-tectal progenitors by its tectal/dorsal midbrain patterning features, especially pax3/7 and dmbx1 gene expression.


```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Cycling ventricular-zone progenitor program
    "mki67", "pcna", "ccnd1", "cdk1", "cdk2", "plk1", "top2a",
    "bub1", "nuf2", "kif11", "kif23", "aspm", "anln",
    "mcm2", "mcm7", "pole", "pole2", "prim2", "dnmt1", "brip1", "bard1",

    # Radial glia identity
    "notch1a", "her8.2", "foxn4", "nr2e1", "sox2",
   
    # Dorsal midbrain / tectal progenitor patterning
    "pax7a", "pax7b", "pax3a", "dmbx1a", "dmbx1b",
    "otx2b", "zic3", "zic6", "tenm3", "plxnb3", "efemp1",

    # Neurogenic but progenitor-biased state
    "sox11b", "myt1a", "ebf2", "bcl11aa", "tox", "cbfa2t2",

    # Growth factor / morphogen responsiveness
    "ctnnb1", "fsta", "fstl1a"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```


## Cluster 1: Telencephalic / anterior forebrain ventricular zone radial glia

One-line identity: Ventricular radial glia / neural progenitors of the anterior forebrain, dominated by core radial glia and progenitor features as well as patterning genes from the telencephalic and preoptic regions (Anneser et al., 2024; Ganz et al., 2012; Jurisch-Yaksi et al., 2020; März et al., 2010; Umeda et al., 2024; Viktorin et al., 2008).  
 
**Key evidence**

  • Core ventricular radial glia / progenitor program: slc1a3b, id4, notch1b, her8.2, sox2, gfap, nes,
  fgfr3, fgfrl1a, fgfr4, lin28ab
    → These genes support ventricular radial glia / neural stem-progenitor identity. 
 
  • Strong telencephalic regional patterning signature: foxg1a, emx2, emx3, fezf1, fezf2, lhx2b, lhx5, pax6b,
  zbtb18, zbtb20, wnt8b
   → These genes support a telencephalic regional annotation: foxg1a is a canonical telencephalic regulator,
   emx genes support pallial forebrain identity, and pallial/subpallial molecular maps in zebrafish use emx,
   dlx, fezf, and foxg1-family logic to define forebrain territories.  
  
  • Ventral / preoptic / anterior forebrain signature: nkx2.4a, nkx2.4b, vax1, vax2, rx3
   → These genes support anterior ventral forebrain / preoptic-hypothalamic proximity and imply that this
   cluster may capture a broader anterior forebrain VZ population rather than a strictly telencephalon-only
   radial glia class.  
  
  • Radial-glia-associated signaling and niche cues: reln, epha2a, epha7, sema3d, robo1, rgma, wnt7ba,
  wnt7bb, wnt8b, aldh1a2
   → These genes fit a ventricular progenitor niche that is still actively patterning the surrounding
   forebrain, rather than a terminal support-glia state. In this context they reinforce a developmental
   forebrain VZ identity.  

**Decision rule:** 

The combination of ventricular radial glia markers with a foxg1a/emx/fezf/lhx/pax6 telencephalic patterning program and nkx2.4/rx3/vax anterior ventral forebrain/preoptic region program supports the annotation as telencephalic/anterior forebrain radial glia

**Distinguishing note:** 

This cluster is defined by a forebrain-specific ventricular zone identity rather than a generic radial glia state or alternative regional progenitor population. The key distinction is the co-occurrence of canonical radial glia markers (slc1a3b, gfap, notch1b, her8.2, and sox2) with a dense telencephalic transcriptional program (foxg1a, emx2/emx3, fezf1/2, lhx2b, pax6b, and zbtb18).

```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Core ventricular radial glia / progenitor program
    "slc1a3b", "id4", "notch1b", "her8.2", "sox2", "gfap", 
    "nes", "fgfr3", "fgfrl1a", "fgfr4", "lin28ab",

    # Telencephalic regional patterning
    "foxg1a", "emx2", "emx3", "fezf1", "fezf2",
    "lhx2b", "lhx5", "pax6b", "zbtb18", "zbtb20", "wnt8b",

    # Ventral / preoptic / anterior forebrain signature
    "nkx2.4a", "nkx2.4b", "vax1", "vax2", "rx3",

    # Radial glia niche / signaling environment
    "reln", "epha2a", "epha7", "sema3d", "robo1", "rgma",
    "wnt7ba", "wnt7bb", "aldh1a2"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```

## Cluster 2: Astrocytes

One-line identity: Mature parenchymal astrocytes defined by strong neurotransmitter-clearance, metabolic-support, and gliovascular-coupling programs. This cluster expresses canonical astrocytic transporter and glutamine-synthetase genes without a dominant expression of ventricular zone radial glia genes (Anneser et al., 2024; J. Chen et al., 2020; Grupp et al., 2010; Luo et al., 2023).  
 
**Key evidence**

  • Core astrocyte homeostatic and neurotransmitter-clearance machinery: slc1a2b, slc7a10a, slc7a10b,
  slc6a13, slc6a11b, slc6a1b, slc6a9, slc38a3a, glula, glulb, mgll, aqp4, kcnj13, slc8a2a, slc4a4a, ca4a
    → This cluster is strongly enriched for genes expected in mature astrocytes that buffer glutamate, GABA,
    glycine, ions, water, and metabolic intermediates. The combination of EAAT2-like glutamate uptake,
    glutamine synthetase, inhibitory neurotransmitter uptake, and osmotic/ionic regulators supports a
    differentiated astrocyte identity centered on parenchymal homeostasis rather than progenitor maintenance.
    Chen et al. specifically identified zebrafish astrocytes expressing glast/slc1a3b, slc1a2b, glutamine
    synthetase, and slc6a11b, providing direct zebrafish support for this transporter-rich astrocytic
    program.  
    
  • Astrocyte extracellular-matrix and vascular-coupling program: mfge8a, megf10, tspan18b, vegfba, vcam1b,
  robo4, gpc5b, cspg5a, cspg5b, fgfbp3, angptl4, slco1e1
    → These genes support astrocytes that interact with extracellular matrix, vasculature, and neighboring
    neuronal elements. The DEG profile is enriched for trophic, adhesive, and vascular-associated molecules
    rather than epithelial or ventricular lining genes, fitting parenchymal astrocytes with gliovascular and
    synapse-adjacent support roles. 

  • Mature astrocytic metabolic-support state: glula, glulb, mgll, hkdc1, psat1, me1, dhrs3b, acer4, acad11,
  acss2l, gpam, pfkfb4a
    → This cluster contains a strong metabolic-support signature consistent with astrocytic roles in
    glutamate–glutamine cycling, lipid handling, redox buffering, and energetic support of neurons. This is
    more consistent with differentiated astrocytes than with cycling radial glia or immature progenitors. 

**Decision rule:** 

The combined presence of strong astrocytic neurotransmitter-uptake genes, glutamine synthetase, metabolic-support pathways, and gliovascular/ECM-associated genes, together with the absence of a strong cycling radial glia signature, supports annotation as mature parenchymal astrocytes.

**Distinguishing note:** 

This cluster is distinguished from ventricular radial glia by its much stronger homeostatic transporter and metabolic program, especially slc1a2b, slc6a11b, slc6a13, slc6a9, slc38a3a, glula/glulb, and aqp4-like astrocytic support functions. It is also more parenchymal and support-oriented than progenitor-like glia, with greater emphasis on neurotransmitter clearance, vascular coupling, and extracellular interaction than on stem-cell maintenance or neurogenic cell-cycle activity.


```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Core astrocyte neurotransmitter-clearance / homeostasis
    "slc1a2b", "slc7a10a", "slc7a10b", "slc6a13", "slc6a11b",
    "slc6a1b", "slc6a9", "slc38a3a", "glula", "glulb",
    "mgll", "aqp4", "kcnj13", "slc8a2a", "slc4a4a", "ca4a",

    # ECM / vascular-coupling / astrocyte interaction program
    "mfge8a", "megf10", "tspan18b", "vegfba", "vcam1b", "robo4",
    "gpc5b", "cspg5a", "cspg5b", "fgfbp3", "angptl4", "slco1e1",

    # Metabolic-support program
    "hkdc1", "psat1", "me1", "dhrs3b", "acer4",
    "acad11", "acss2l", "gpam", "pfkfb4a"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```
## Cluster 3: Cerebellar ventricular-zone radial glia (MHB-associated)

One-line identity: Cerebellar ventricular-zone radial glia associated with the midbrain–hindbrain boundary (MHB), defined by strong FGF organizer signaling and progenitor-state markers (Gibbs et al., 2017; Hirate & Okamoto, 2006; Kaslin et al., 2013; Pose-Méndez et al., 2023).
 
**Key evidence**

  • MHB / cerebellar organizer-patterning program:cnpy1, fgf3, fgf8a, fgf8b, fgf10a, fgf22, fgf24, fgfrl1a,
  crabp1a
    → This cluster shows a clear FGF-linked organizer signature centered on genes associated with the
    zebrafish midbrain–hindbrain boundary and adjacent cerebellar territory. 
 
  • Cerebellar / MHB regional identity genes: dmbx1b, lhx2b, zic2a, tbx2b, tbx3a, foxn4, gbx2, otx2b
    → These genes support a patterned hindbrain–cerebellar progenitor territory rather than a generic glial
    state. In zebrafish, the cerebellum develops from dorsal rhombomere 1 under organizer influence from the
    MHB, so this combination is most consistent with cerebellar progenitor-zone localization.  
 
  • Immature glial / progenitor features: pdgfra, cspg4ba, smoc1, smoc2, cntfr, nes
    → The cluster contains genes consistent with immature glial or progenitor-zone support cells, fitting a
    progenitor-associated cerebellar glial population.  
 
  • Developmental signaling and boundary-associated guidance: efna5b, epha2b, nrp2b, rgmd, plxdc2b
    → These genes encode components of Eph/ephrin, semaphorin/neuropilin, and BMP-associated signaling
    systems that mediate cell segregation, positional identity, and axon guidance, genes supporting the
    annotation of a progenitor population embedded in a regionally patterned, boundary-associated
    developmental environment.

**Decision rule:**

The combined presence of cnpy1 with multiple FGF-pathway and cerebellar/MHB-associated genes supports annotation as cerebellar progenitor-zone glia.

**Distinguishing note:**

This cluster is distinguished from other ventricular-zone glia by its MHB/cerebellar organizer signature, especially cnpy1 and fgf genes. It is distinguished from mature astrocytes by its progenitor-like developmental profile and weaker homeostatic transporter signature.


```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # MHB / cerebellar organizer-patterning program
    "cnpy1", "fgf3", "fgf8a", "fgf8b", "fgf10a", "fgf22",
    "fgf24", "fgfrl1a", "crabp1a",

    # Cerebellar / MHB regional identity
    "dmbx1b", "lhx2b", "zic2a", "tbx2b", "tbx3a",
    "foxn4", "gbx2", "otx2b",

    # Immature glial / progenitor features
    "pdgfra", "cspg4ba", "smoc1", "smoc2", "cntfr", "nes",

    # Boundary-associated guidance / signaling
    "efna5b", "epha2b", "nrp2b", "rgmd", "plxdc2b"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```
## Cluster 4: Ventral hypothalamic tanycyte-like radial glia

One-line identity: Specialized ventricular radial glia of the ventral hypothalamus with a tanycyte-like profile, defined by ventricular glial markers, strong ventral hypothalamic patterning genes, prominent Shh/Wnt signaling, extracellular matrix and guidance programs, and a ciliogenesis module consistent with a ventricular lining cell specialized for hypothalamic niche signaling rather than a generic radial glial or ependymal state (Ceriani & Whitlock, 2021; D’Gama et al., 2021; Duncan et al., 2016; Male et al., 2020; Manoli & Driever, 2014; Norton et al., 2005; Sedykh et al., 2018).  
 
**Key evidence**

  • Tanycyte / ventricular radial glia core markers: ptn, pkd1b, prom1a, lama2, hapln1a, sparcl1, nrcama,
  gpc5b
    → This cluster shows a strong ventricular glial profile defined by apical-surface markers and
    extracellular matrix components associated with the ventricular niche. In zebrafish, tanycytes represent
    a specialized subtype of hypothalamic ventricular radial glia with persistent progenitor capacity and
    niche-associated signaling functions.

  • Ventral hypothalamic patterning program: foxa, foxa1, foxa2, shha, shhb, nkx6.1, lmx1ba, lmx1bb, arxa,
  rfx4
    → These genes strongly support ventral hypothalamic identity. This patterning program is characteristic
    of ventral midline progenitor domains from which tanycyte populations arise, distinguishing this cluster
    from dorsal or non-hypothalamic radial glia.
 
  • Posterior / ventral hypothalamic signaling environment: wnt4, wnt4b, wnt11, wnt16, efnb3a, ntn1b,
  cxcl12a, slit1a, slit2, slit3
    → The transcriptome is enriched for secreted morphogens and guidance cues, consistent with a
    signaling-active ventricular niche. This profile supports a tanycyte identity, as these cells function as
    locally signaling progenitors that regulate hypothalamic neurogenesis and tissue organization.
 
  • Ciliogenesis and ventricular specialization: foxj1a, dnah2, dnah7, cfap100, cfap298, urp2, cdkn1ba
    → This cluster carries a clear ciliogenesis program consistent with ventricular-surface specialization.
    Tanycytes are ciliated ventricular radial glia so the cooccurrence of foxj1a and axonemal dynein
    components (dnah and cfap genes) motile cilia genes with ventral hypothalamic patterning and
    tanycyte-associated niche features supports a specialized tanycyte identity rather than a purely
    ependymal cell type.
 
  • Secretory / niche-regulatory and neuroendocrine-adjacent features: pam, nr4a3, igf2b, cxcl12a, scube1,
  scube3
    → These genes support a signaling-active ventricular niche population with neuroendocrine-adjacent
    regulatory capacity. The presence of peptide-processing enzymes (pam), growth factors (igf2b), chemokines
    (cxcl12a), and secreted signaling modulators (scube genes) is consistent with tanycytes, which function
    as locally signaling ventricular cells that regulate hypothalamic neurogenesis and neuroendocrine
    circuits.

**Decision rule:** 

The combined presence of a ventricular radial glia scaffold, strong ventral hypothalamic foxa–shh–lmx1b–nkx logic, and a ciliogenesis module supports annotation as ventral hypothalamic tanycyte-like radial glia.  

**Distinguishing note:**

This cluster is distinguished from broader hypothalamic ventricular radial glia by its stronger ventral floor-plate-like hypothalamic patterning signature and from more generic ependymal cells by its retention of hypothalamic niche-signaling genes such as shha, shhb, wnt4/wnt4b, cxcl12a, and slit family members. Functionally, these cells most likely represent a specialized ventricular glial niche at the ventral hypothalamic surface.  

```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Tanycyte / ventricular radial glia core markers
    "ptn", "pkd1b", "prom1a", "lama2", "hapln1a",
    "sparcl1", "nrcama", "gpc5b",

    # Ventral hypothalamic patterning
    "foxa", "foxa1", "foxa2", "shha", "shhb",
    "nkx6.1", "lmx1ba", "lmx1bb", "arxa", "rfx4",

    # Posterior / ventral hypothalamic signaling
    "wnt4", "wnt4b", "wnt11", "wnt16",
    "efnb3a", "ntn1b", "cxcl12a",
    "slit1a", "slit2", "slit3",

    # Ciliogenesis / ventricular specialization
    "foxj1a", "dnah2", "dnah7", "cfap100", "cfap298", "urp2", "cdkn1ba",

    # Secretory / niche-regulatory features
    "pam", "nr4a3", "igf2b", "scube1", "scube3"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```
## Cluster 5: Ependymal dorsal VZ radial glia

One-line identity: Dorsal ventricular zone radial glia transitioning into a multiciliated ependymal lineage, defined by a strong FOXJ1/ciliogenesis program, dorsal roof-plate patterning code, and Wnt/BMP-rich ventricular signaling consistent with roof-plate–derived ventricular epithelium (D’Gama et al., 2021; Elsen et al., 2008; Kondrychyn et al., 2013; Sunmonu et al., 2011; Yamaguchi et al., 2018).  
 
**Key evidence**

  • Multiciliated ependymal differentiation program: foxj1b, sspo, prom1a, dnaaf1, dnaaf3, dnah5, dnah7,
  cfap91, ift88, gas8, ttc21b
    → This is the strongest signal in the cluster. The combination of foxj1b with broad axonemal dynein,
    CFAP, tektin, and intraflagellar transport machinery supports ventricular cells actively engaged in
    motile-cilia differentiation, which is a defining feature of zebrafish ependymal lineages.  
  
  • Dorsal VZ / roof-plate positional program: zic1, zic2a, zic4, zic5, zic6, msx1b, lmx1ba, lmx1bb, rxrab,
  pax2b
    → The dense Zic/Msx dorsal patterning code strongly supports dorsal ventricular origin. In zebrafish,
    Zic1 and Zic4 are specifically linked to roof-plate specification and hindbrain ventricle morphogenesis,
    which fits this cluster much better than a generic ventricular glial label.  
  
  • Roof-plate signaling environment rather than generic glial maintenance: wnt1, wnt3, wnt4, wnt7ba, fgf8b,
  bmp6, bmper, acvr1ba, axin2, cnpy1
    → This cluster is enriched for dorsal organizer-style morphogen signaling, especially Wnt/BMP and
    FGF-associated genes, which is characteristic of roof-plate or dorsal ventricular epithelium. This is not
    the transcriptional profile expected for broad radial glia maintenance alone.  
  
  • Ventricular epithelial / basal lamina organization: sparc, col15a1a, col16a1, col4a5, frem1a, cdh6,
  cldn7a, cadm1b, tgfbr3, adamts10
    → These genes support apical-basal epithelial organization, extracellular matrix assembly, and
    ventricular surface specialization, consistent with developing ependymal ventricular cells rather than
    migratory progenitors or mature parenchymal glia.  
  
  • Radial glia / progenitor heritage: sox2, vim, her4.1, fgfr3
    → These genes indicate that the population still retains ventricular progenitor ancestry, but the cluster
    is no longer best described as generic radial glia because the ciliogenesis and epithelial specialization
    modules are much stronger.  

**Decision rule:** 

The combined presence of foxj1b-driven multiciliation, extensive motile-cilia structural genes, strong dorsal Zic/Msx patterning, and roof-plate Wnt/BMP signaling supports annotation as ependymal dorsal VZ radial glia, best interpreted as a dorsal ventricular radial glia-to-ependymal transition state.

**Distinguishing note:**

This cluster is distinguished from hypothalamic tanycyte-like ventricular glia by its dorsal Zic/Msx/roof-plate patterning code and robust FOXJ1 multiciliation program, and from broader ventricular radial glia by its much stronger ependymal differentiation machinery and ventricular epithelial ECM signature. Functionally, these cells appear to represent dorsal ventricular glia committing to a multiciliated ependymal identity.

```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Multiciliated ependymal differentiation
    "foxj1b", "sspo", "prom1a",
    "dnaaf1", "dnah5", "dnah7",
    "ift88",

    # Dorsal VZ / roof-plate patterning
    "zic1", "zic2a", "zic4",
    "msx1b", "lmx1ba", "pax2b",

    # Roof-plate signaling environment
    "wnt1", "wnt3", "wnt7ba",
    "fgf8b", "bmp6", "axin2", "cnpy1",

    # Ventricular epithelial / ECM organization
    "sparc", "col15a1a", "col4a5",
    "frem1a", "cdh6", "cldn7a",

    # Residual radial glia heritage
    "sox2", "vim", "LOC103040661", "fgfr3" # "LOC103040661" = "her4.1"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```
## Clusters 6/11: OPCs

One-line identity: Oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) in an early, highly interactive state, defined by core OPC lineage markers together with strong neuronal communication, synaptic adhesion, neurotransmitter receptor, and excitability programs, consistent with OPCs that are actively sensing and integrating neural activity rather than fully differentiated myelinating oligodendrocytes (Akay et al., 2021; Bromley-Coolidge et al., 2024; Kuhn et al., 2019; J. Li et al., 2024; Marisca et al., 2020; Ravanelli et al., 2018).  
 
**Key evidence**

  • Core OPC lineage program: olig1, olig2 ,cspg4, qkia, lingo1a, lingo1b, gfra4b, ppp1r14bb, sox10
    → This cluster contains a clear oligodendrocyte-lineage precursor signature, especially olig1 and cspg4,
    which strongly supports OPC identity rather than neuronal or astroglial annotation. In zebrafish,
    persistent OPC populations are molecularly distinct from differentiating oligodendrocytes and cspg4 is a
    conserved OPC marker.  
  
  • Synaptic adhesion and neuron-contact machinery:  nlgn1, nlgn2a, nlgn2b, nlgn3a, lrrtm2, lrfn1, lrfn2b,
  lrfn5b, cntnap5b, dscamb, cadm3, sdk2a, sdk2b, ptprdb, ptprub, ptprua
    → This DEG profile is heavily enriched for synapse-like recognition and adhesion genes, consistent with
    OPCs making structured contacts with axons and responding to neuronal signals. This interpretation
    matches zebrafish work showing oligodendroglial cells use synaptic proteins and neuron-glia contacts
    during myelin-related development.  
    
  • Neurotransmitter receptor and excitability-rich state:vgria1a, gria1b, gria4a, grik2, grik4, grik5,
  grin3ba, gabbr1b, gabrb2a, htr1d, kcnj6, kcnd1, kcnn3, kcnip3a, cacng2a, cacng4a, cacng8a, clcn2a, asic1b,
  asic1c
    → These genes support a physiologically responsive OPC state. OPCs are known to receive synaptic input
    and exhibit activity-dependent calcium signaling. Zebrafish studies specifically support neuron-OPC
    synapses as functionally important for later myelin sheath formation.  
  
  • Axon-guidance, migration, and surveillance features: sema5a, sema4ba, sema6ba, sema6e, efna3a, plxnb1a,
  hapln3, col27a1a, adamts6, ptprk, ptprfa, ptprma
    → These genes fit a motile, environment-sensing precursor rather than a stable mature oligodendrocyte,
    supporting the interpretation of OPCs navigating and sampling axonal territory while remaining
    developmentally plastic.  

**Decision rule:** 

The combined presence of olig1/cspg4 OPC markers, absence of a dominant mature-myelin program, and very strong synaptic adhesion, receptor, and excitability modules supports annotation as early interactive OPCs.

**Distinguishing note:** 

This cluster is distinguished from more mature oligodendrocyte-lineage cells by its much stronger neuron-contact and receptor-rich profile, and from non-glial neuronal clusters by its retained OPC lineage core. Functionally, these cells appear to represent OPCs that are still highly engaged in axon sensing, synaptic communication, and activity-dependent fate regulation.  

```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Core OPC lineage program
    "olig1", "olig2", "cspg4", "qkia", "lingo1a", "lingo1b",
    "gfra4b", "ppp1r14bb", "sox10",

    # Synaptic adhesion / neuron-contact machinery
    "nlgn1", "nlgn2a", "nlgn2b", "nlgn3a",
    "lrrtm2", "lrfn1", "lrfn2b", "lrfn5b",
    "cntnap5b", "dscamb", "cadm3", "sdk2a", "sdk2b",
    "ptprdb", "ptprub", "ptprua",

    # Neurotransmitter receptor / excitability-rich state
    "gria1a", "gria1b", "gria4a", "grik2", "grik4", "grik5",
    "grin3ba", "gabbr1b", "gabrb2a", "htr1d",
    "kcnj6", "kcnd1", "kcnn3", "kcnip3a",
    "cacng2a", "cacng4a", "cacng8a",
    "clcn2a", "asic1b", "asic1c",

    # Axon-guidance / migration / surveillance
    "sema5a", "sema4ba", "sema6ba", "sema6e",
    "efna3a", "plxnb1a", "hapln3", "col27a1a",
    "adamts6", "ptprk", "ptprfa", "ptprma"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```
## Cluster 7: Early oligodendrocytes

One-line identity: Early differentiating oligodendrocytes transitioning out of the OPC state, defined by retained oligodendrocyte-lineage markers together with strong pre-myelinating and early myelin programs, plus persistent axon-contact and receptor-rich features (Y. Chen et al., 2009; Kuhn et al., 2019; Santos-Ledo et al., 2023; Takada et al., 2010; Treichel & Hines, 2018).
 
**Key evidence**

  • Core oligodendrocyte-lineage identity: olig2, sox10, nkx2.2a, myrf, zeb2a, zeb2b, st18, sox6
    → This cluster is firmly within the oligodendrocyte lineage. The combination of sox10, olig2, nkx2.2a,
    myrf, and zeb2 factors places it developmentally beyond a generic OPC state and into an actively
    differentiating oligodendrocyte trajectory.
 
  • Early OL / premyelinating program: gpr17, bcas1, mag, mbpb, mbpa, abca2, plp2b, lingo1a, myrf
    → These are the strongest features distinguishing this cluster from OPCs. Gpr17 and bcas1 are classic
    transitional early OL markers, while mag and mbp-family genes indicate that myelin differentiation has
    begun but is not yet fully mature.
  
  • Emerging myelin structural identity without a fully mature compact-myelin state:  mbpb, mbpa, mag, plp2b,
  abca2, cldn19
    → This cluster has clearly initiated myelin gene expression, which argues against an OPC annotation. At
    the same time, the profile still looks earlier than fully mature myelinating oligodendrocytes because the
    program is mixed with strong transitional, morphogenetic, and signaling genes.
 
  • Persistent axon-glia interaction and adhesion machinery: cadm4, cntn1a, nfasca, opcml, tnr, vcanb,
  plxna3, plxnb2b, sema4ga, sema3b, sema5a
    → These genes support active axon engagement, process extension, and axoglial contact formation. That
    fits an early oligodendrocyte state that is beginning to establish stable interactions with axons during
    pre-myelinating differentiation.

  • Receptor-rich, still-responsive transitional state: gria3a, grik3, grm1a, grm5b, kcnh5a, kcnj10a, gpr17,
  gfra3, gfra4a, gpr52
    → Compared with a more mature OL state, this cluster still shows substantial signaling responsiveness and
    environmental sensing, consistent with newly differentiating OLs that have not yet fully shut down
    precursor-like interaction programs.

**Decision rule:** 

The presence of oligodendrocyte-lineage TFs together with strong transitional early OL markers and clear onset of myelin-gene expression supports annotation as early oligodendrocytes rather than OPCs.

**Distinguishing note:** 

This cluster is more mature than OPCs because it expresses a much stronger early myelin and differentiation program, especially myrf, gpr17, bcas1, mag, and mbp-family genes. In contrast, the more OPC-like state is dominated by precursor identity and neural interaction genes without this degree of myelin initiation.

```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Core oligodendrocyte-lineage identity
    "olig2", "sox10", "nkx2.2a", "myrf", "zeb2a", "zeb2b", "st18", "sox6",

    # Early OL / premyelinating program
    "gpr17", "bcas1", "mag", "mbpb", "mbpa", "abca2", "plp2b", "lingo1a",

    # Emerging myelin structural identity
    "cldn19",

    # Axon-glia interaction / adhesion
    "cadm4", "cntn1a", "nfasca", "opcml", "tnr", "vcanb",
    "plxna3", "plxnb2b", "sema4ga", "sema3b", "sema5a",

    # Receptor-rich transitional state
    "gria3a", "grik3", "grm1a", "grm5b",
    "kcnh5a", "kcnj10a", "gfra3", "gfra4a", "gpr52"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```
## Cluster 8: Hypothalamic Ventricular Zone radial glia

One-line identity: Ventral hypothalamic / ventral diencephalic radial glia lining the ventricular zone, defined by a Shh-responsive ventral forebrain patterning program together with radial glial markers and ventricular-surface signaling features, most strongly supported by nkx2.1 / nkx2.2-family, shha, foxa-family, and sim1a-associated hypothalamic markers (Diotel et al., 2010, 2015; Duncan et al., 2016; Male et al., 2020; Manoli & Driever, 2014; Mathieu et al., 2002; Ryu & Wolf, 2013). 
 
**Key evidence**

  • Definitive ventral hypothalamic / ventral diencephalic patterning program/ Hypothalamic lineage support:
  foxa, foxa1, foxa2, shha, shhb, nkx2.1, nkx2.2a, nkx2.2b, sim1a
   → Hedgehog signaling is a core pathway in hypothalamic regionalization and nkx2.1/nkx2.4-family genes are
   directly required for hypothalamic development and basal hypothalamic patterning. Sim1a is also linked to
   hypothalamic and posterior tubercular differentiation programs and is required to form the posterior
   hypothalamus.

  • Radial glia / ventricular glial identity: fabp7a, s100b, glula, gpm6ba, gfod1
   → These genes support a glial ventricular-zone identity rather than a neuronal cluster. In this context,
   the regional patterning program sits on top of a radial glia-like state, making the best interpretation
   hypothalamic VZ radial glia rather than differentiated hypothalamic neurons.

  • Ventricular-zone signaling / niche features consistent with hypothalamic RG: wnt11, cxcl12b, sulf1,
  slc6a11b, slc6a1b, slc1a2b, itpr3
   → These genes fit a signaling-responsive ventricular niche rather than a mature parenchymal glial
   population, supporting a specialized ventricular surface / progenitor-zone state.
 
  • Axon guidance / morphogen-routing environment expected near ventral hypothalamic ventricular surfaces:
  ntn1b, slit1a, sema3e, rgma, efna1b, celsr2
   → These genes are consistent with a ventricular organizer-like or morphogen-routing niche in developing
   ventral forebrain tissue. They support the idea that this is a patterned ventricular glial population
   helping shape local hypothalamic environment rather than a generic astrocyte class.
 
  • Glial transport and signaling responsiveness consistent with VZ physiology: slc6a11b, slc6a9, slc6a1b,
  slc8a1b, itpr3
   → These transporters and signaling genes are compatible with ventricular glial physiology and
   neurotransmitter handling, supporting a specialized radial glial population that is responsive to local
   circuit and niche signals rather than a purely structural epithelial population. The presence of
   astroglial/radial-glial transport genes alongside hypothalamic patterning genes reinforces a ventricular
   glial interpretation.  

**Decision rule:**

The combination of nkx2.1 / nkx2.2-family, shha/shhb, and foxa-family ventral patterning genes with clear radial glial markers supports annotation as hypothalamic ventricular zone radial glia. 

**Distinguishing note:** 

This cluster is distinguished from generic ventricular glia by its strong ventral hypothalamic patterning code, especially shha, foxa-family,nkx2-family. It is also distinguishable from the more specialized tanycyte-like cluster because the strongest evidence here is for patterned hypothalamic VZ radial glia, not a more terminal tanycyte transport/secretory state.

```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Ventral hypothalamic / ventral diencephalic patterning
    "foxa", "foxa1", "foxa2", "shha", "shhb",
    "nkx2.1", "nkx2.2a", "nkx2.2b", "sim1a",

    # Radial glia / ventricular glial identity
    "fabp7a", "s100b", "glula", "gpm6ba", "gfod1",

    # Ventricular-zone signaling / niche features
    "wnt11", "cxcl12b", "sulf1", "slc6a11b", "slc6a1b", "slc1a2b", "itpr3",

    # Axon guidance / morphogen-routing environment
    "ntn1b", "slit1a", "sema3e", "rgma", "efna1b", "celsr2",

    # Glial transport / signaling responsiveness
    "slc6a9", "slc8a1b"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```
## Cluster 9: Myelinating oligodendrocytes

One-line identity: Mature, actively myelinating oligodendrocytes, defined by a dense myelin-structural program together with oligodendrocyte-lineage transcription factors and paranodal/junctional myelin components, consistent with differentiated CNS oligodendrocytes rather than OPCs or early premyelinating (Bai et al., 2014; Brösamle & Halpern, 2002; Collins et al., 2025; H. Li et al., 2007; Münzel et al., 2012).
 
**Key evidence**

  • Strong compact-myelin structural program: mbpa, mbpb, mpz, mag, plp1a, plp1b, cldnk, cldn19
    → This cluster is dominated by canonical myelin genes, indicating active myelin sheath production rather
    than precursor identity.
 
  • Oligodendrocyte-lineage transcriptional identity: sox10, myrf, qki2, st18, prox1a, rundc3aa
   → These genes anchor the cluster within the oligodendrocyte lineage and support a differentiated
   myelinating state.

  • Mature myelin membrane specialization: nfascb, nfasca, gjc2, tjp1a, cd9b
   → Enrichment of junctional and paranodal membrane-associated genes supports organized sheath architecture
   and axon-glial domain specialization.

  • Differentiated oligodendrocyte maturation program: enpp6, bcas1, cd82a, aspa, slc44a1b, acsl1b, elovl7a
   → These genes support late-stage oligodendrocyte differentiation, membrane lipid remodeling, and myelin
   maintenance.
  
**Decision rule:**

The combined presence of very strong CNS myelin structural genes, oligodendrocyte-lineage regulators, and junctional/paranodal myelin components supports annotation as myelinating oligodendrocytes.  

**Distinguishing note:** 

This cluster is distinguished from OPCs and early OLs by its much heavier compact-myelin program, especially mbpa/mbpb, mpz, mag, plp1a/plp1b, cldnk, cldn19, nfascb, and gjc2, indicating established myelin production rather than merely oligodendrocyte-lineage commitment.  

```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Strong compact-myelin structural program
    "mbpa", "mbpb", "mpz", "mag",
    "plp1a", "plp1b", "cldnk", "cldn19",

    # Oligodendrocyte-lineage transcriptional identity
    "sox10", "myrf", "qki2", "st18",
    "prox1a", "rundc3aa",

    # Mature myelin membrane specialization
    "nfascb", "nfasca", "gjc2", "tjp1a", "cd9b",

    # Differentiated oligodendrocyte maturation program
    "enpp6", "bcas1", "cd82a", "aspa",
    "slc44a1b", "acsl1b", "elovl7a"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```

## Cluster 10: Microglia

One-line identity: Brain-resident microglia with a canonical zebrafish myeloid/microglial program, defined by csf1r-dependent microglial identity genes, irf8/spi1 lineage regulators, and strong lysosomal-phagocytic machinery, consistent with differentiated microglia rather than non-resident macrophages or other glia (Herbomel et al., 2001; Kuil et al., 2020; Mazzolini et al., 2020; Oosterhof et al., 2018; Peri & Nüsslein-Volhard, 2008; Shiau et al., 2015; Silva et al., 2021).  
 
**Key evidence**

  • Definitive microglial / myeloid identity: csf1ra, csf1rb, ptprc, cd68, mpeg1* (LOC103034161), lcp1,
  coro1a
     → This is the clearest anchor for the cluster. In zebrafish, microglia are defined by macrophage-lineage
     identity and depend strongly on csf1r signaling for normal brain colonization and maintenance;
     mpeg1-positive brain macrophages are the canonical population used to mark zebrafish
     microglia/macrophages.  
 
  • Microglial lineage-specifying transcription factors: irf8, spi1a, mafba, irf5
     → These genes strongly support resident microglial identity rather than generic immune contamination:
     irf8 is a key zebrafish regulator required for normal microglial development, and spi1/pu.1 is a core 
     myeloid lineage regulator. 
 
  • Strong phagocytic and lysosomal program: ctsla, ctsba, ctsc, ctsh, ctsz, lgmn, dnase2, mcoln1a, atp6v1ba,
  tcirg1b
     → This cluster is heavily enriched for endolysosomal and degradative machinery, which fits the
     scavenging and phagocytic role of zebrafish microglia in the CNS at 6 dpf. 
 
  • Immune surveillance and signaling receptors: fcer1g, tnfrsf1b, il10rb, syk, btk, inpp5d, ptpn6, lyn,
  pik3cg
     → These genes indicate an activated innate immune signaling repertoire typical of microglia, including
     Fc-receptor signaling, cytokine responsiveness, and immune phosphatase/kinase modules associated with
     resident brain macrophages.  
 
  • Lipid-handling and immune-homeostatic microglial program: apoc1, apoeb, csf1rb, mpeg1, ptprc
     → In addition to core myeloid markers, this cluster expresses conserved microglial lipid-handling and
     immune-associated genes, including apoc1 and apoeb. This transcriptional profile is consistent with
     resident CNS microglia engaged in immune surveillance and lipid metabolism rather than peripheral
     leukocytes.
 
  • Motility and surveillance-associated cytoskeletal machinery: rac2, myo1g, fmnl1a, bin2b, arhgap15, actr2b
     → These genes support a highly motile, actin-remodeling immune cell state, consistent with the dynamic
     surveillance behavior of microglia in zebrafish brain tissue.  

**Decision rule:** 

The combined presence of csf1r-pathway genes, irf8/spi1 myeloid regulators, conserved zebrafish microglia markers, and a dominant lysosomal-phagocytic program supports annotation as microglia.  

**Distinguishing note:**

This cluster is distinguished from other glia by its strong immune/phagocytic machinery and from broader peripheral macrophage-like populations by the specific zebrafish microglial signature centered on csf1r dependence, irf8, and conserved resident microglia markers such as apoc1/apoeb.  

mpeg1 = "LOC103034161"
```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Definitive microglial / myeloid identity
    "csf1ra", "csf1rb", "ptprc", "cd68",
    "LOC103034161", "lcp1", "coro1a",

    # Microglial lineage TFs
    "irf8", "spi1a", "mafba", "irf5",

    # Phagocytic / lysosomal program
    "ctsla", "ctsba", "ctsc", "ctsh", "ctsz",
    "lgmn", "dnase2", "mcoln1a", "atp6v1ba", "tcirg1b",

    # Immune surveillance / signaling receptors
    "fcer1g", "tnfrsf1b", "il10rb", "syk", "btk",
    "inpp5d", "ptpn6", "lyn", "pik3cg",

    # Lipid-handling / immune-homeostatic program
    "apoc1", "apoeb",

    # Motility / surveillance cytoskeletal machinery
    "rac2", "myo1g", "fmnl1a", "bin2b", "arhgap15", "actr2b"
    
  )
) + RotatedAxis()
```
## Cluster 12: Multiciliated ependymal cells

One-line identity: A mature ventricular ependymal cell population with a FOXJ1-driven motile-cilia program and apical ventricular-surface specialization, consistent with multiciliated ependymal cells rather than radial glia, tanycytes, or generic epithelial cells (Olstad et al., 2019; Pathak et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2022; Xie et al., 2023; Yamaguchi et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2020).
 
**Key evidence**

  • Definitive multiciliated ependymal program: foxj1b, tp73, dnah1, dnah2, dnah3, dnah5, dnah5l, dnah6,
  dnah7, dnah9, dnah10, dnah12, dnai1.2, dnai3, rsph1, rsph10b, ccdc39, ccdc40, hydin, tekt1, ttll6, ttll10,
  cfap45, cfap53, cfap54, cfap57, cfap58, cfap61,cfap65, cfap91, cfap100, cfap221, cfap299, odad1, odad2,
  odad3, odad4, pacrg, spef2, kif6, kif9, pih1d2
   →  This cluster is dominated by a large motile-cilia and axoneme assembly program characteristic of
   multiciliated ependymal cells: foxj1b and tp73 are core regulators of motile ciliogenesis. Further the
   extensive enrichment of axonemal dyneins (dnah/dnai), radial spoke proteins (rsph), and cilia assembly
   factors (cfap, ccdc, hydin) strongly supports a mature multiciliated ventricular epithelial identity
   rather than radial glia or other neural cell types.
   
  • Ventricular lining / apical specialization: prom2, pkhd1l1.1, cldn15lb, jupa, cgnl1, stx3b
   → These genes support a CSF-facing ventricular lining cell rather than a parenchymal glial population.
 
  • Ciliogenesis and basal body machinery: ift172, ift81, ift80, cep genes, bbs genes, rpgrip1l, ofd1
   → Strong intraflagellar transport and basal body program confirms active and mature cilia assembly,
   consistent with ependymal cells.

**Decision rule:** 

The overwhelming FOXJ1 / motile-cilia program, combined with ventricular epithelial polarity genes and dorsal ventricular signaling features, supports annotation as multiciliated ependymal epithelium.  

**Distinguishing note:**

This cluster is distinguished from radial glia by its massive motile-cilia structural program and epithelial polarity features, and from immature ependymal / pre-ependymal cells by the breadth and intensity of its mature axonemal gene set. 

```{r}
DotPlot(lSeqGlia, features = c(
  
    # Core FOXJ1 / multiciliated ependymal program
    "foxj1b", "tp73",
    "dnah1", "dnah2", "dnah3", "dnah5", "dnah5l", "dnah6",
    "dnah7", "dnah9", "dnah10", "dnah12",
    "dnai1.2", "dnai3",
    "rsph1", "rsph10b",
    "ccdc39", "ccdc40", "hydin",
    "tekt1", "ttll6", "ttll10",
    "cfap45", "cfap53", "cfap54", "cfap57", "cfap58",
    "cfap61", "cfap65", "cfap91", "cfap100", "cfap221", "cfap299",
    "odad1", "odad2", "odad3", "odad4",
    "pacrg", "spef2", "kif6", "kif9", "pih1d2",

    "prom2", "pkhd1l1.1", "cldn15lb", "jupa", "cgnl1", "stx3b",

  )
```

## General labels
Lump radial glia and oligodendrocyte clusters for simplicity
```{r}
lSeqGliaGen <- lSeqGlia

# Named vector for relabeling clusters
cluster_labels <- data.frame(
  
  cluster = 0:12,
  celltype = c(
    "Radial glia", #0
    "Radial glia", #1
    "Astrocytes", #2
    "Radial glia", #3
    "Tanycytes", #4
    "Radial glia", #5
     "OPCs", #6
    "Oligodendrocytes", #7
     "Radial glia", #8
     "Oligodendrocytes", #9
    "Microglia", #10
    "OPCs", #11
    "Ependymal" #12
    
  ))


# Convert Idents to numeric or character to match cluster_labels
cluster_ids <- as.numeric(as.character(Idents(lSeqGliaGen)))

# Join the labels
lSeqGliaGen$celltype <- cluster_labels$celltype[match(cluster_ids, cluster_labels$cluster)]
Idents(lSeqGliaGen) <- lSeqGliaGen$celltype

# Order for plotting
Idents(lSeqGliaGen) <- factor(
  Idents(lSeqGliaGen),
  levels = c("Radial glia","Astrocytes","Tanycytes", "OPCs","Oligodendrocytes","Microglia", "Ependymal")
)
```

```{r}
    Population = factor(population, levels = c("surface", "cave")),
    CellType   = celltype
  )
```
